subsystems.name: Encoding and error-correction layer
subsystems.role: turns ordinary binary data into DNA sequences that can survive being written and read back.
parts: constraint codes that avoid long runs of one base and extreme GC content
address and primer tags for random access

subsystems.name: DNA synthesis
subsystems.role: the writer — builds the strands base by base.
parts: array-based synthesis chips producing many strands at once

subsystems.name: Molecular computing elements
subsystems.role: perform logic through molecular interactions instead of transistors.
parts: enzymes such as polymerases, nickases and restriction enzymes

subsystems.name: Reaction environment
subsystems.role: keeps reactions separate, buffered and controllable.

subsystems.name: Readout
subsystems.role: converts a molecular state back into readable data.

subsystems.name: Automation and fluidics
subsystems.role: makes writing and reading repeatable without constant human handling.

buildSteps.title: Encode the data
buildSteps.detail: Software converts the file into nucleotide sequences, adding parity and constraint codes so errors can later be detected and repaired.

buildSteps.title: Design addressable blocks
buildSteps.detail: The sequence is split into short strands, each flanked by primer tags so a single file or block can be pulled out of the pool without reading everything.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise the strands
buildSteps.detail: Chemical synthesis builds each strand base by base on a solid support or an array chip; enzymatic synthesis is being developed to write longer strands with fewer errors.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and verify
buildSteps.detail: Blocks are joined by ligation or overlap assembly, then sequenced to check them; failures are discarded or re-made.

buildSteps.title: Store the DNA
buildSteps.detail: The pool is dried or encapsulated and kept cool, dark and away from moisture — the conditions under which DNA can persist for a very long time.

buildSteps.title: Retrieve a subset
buildSteps.detail: PCR with the right primer pair amplifies only the addressed blocks, so recovering one file does not require sequencing the whole archive.

buildSteps.title: Sequence
buildSteps.detail: The amplified DNA is read on a high-throughput sequencer, producing raw base calls with error scores.

buildSteps.title: Decode and repair
buildSteps.detail: Software maps reads back to addresses, corrects errors with the parity codes and reconstructs the original file.

buildSteps.title: For computing: run the circuit
buildSteps.detail: Where computation rather than storage is the goal, the strands are mixed so displacement reactions cascade through designed gates, with the output read as fluorescence or a new sequence.

prerequisites.why: array synthesis is inexpensive but error-prone, while accurate column synthesis is slow and costly; archival storage needs both cheap and clean.
reading costs fell by orders of magnitude, which is what makes DNA readout practical at all.

prerequisites.tech: Error-correcting codes for the DNA channel
prerequisites.why: synthesis and sequencing errors are well characterised, and coding schemes that tolerate them have been demonstrated.
DNA computation has been shown since Adleman's 1994 experiment, and strand-displacement circuits of hundreds of gates work in test tubes, but scaling and operation inside cells remain hard.
dry, cool, sealed storage is understood in principle, but standardised archive engineering over decades is not established.

pathway.milestone: laboratory systems that store megabyte-scale data in DNA and molecular circuits that compute in a test tube
pathway.unlocks: proof that the write–store–read loop works end to end.

pathway.milestone: automated write-and-read instruments running many cycles unattended, using enzymatic synthesis
pathway.unlocks: a realistic cost per bit and a realistic throughput for real archives.

pathway.milestone: pilot archival deployments paired with conventional storage, where DNA holds the cold, rarely accessed copy
pathway.unlocks: a role for DNA as a long-lived backup layer rather than a replacement for disks.

pathway.milestone: molecular computers that sense markers inside cells and compute a response
pathway.unlocks: diagnostics and programmable therapeutics that act at the molecular level.
